Human AS3MTd2d3: Exon Skipping and Neural Phenotypes

Source: vignettes/as3mt-splice-variants-demo.Rmd
as3mt-splice-variants-demo.Rmd

What this example compares

This example compares the selected human full-length AS3MT transcript, a paper-defined AS3MTd2d3 reconstruction, and the selected chimpanzee full-length reference. Full-reference exon numbers are retained: the short human model contains E1 and E4–E11. Its transcript ends are reconstructed from the current canonical reference; no stable accession for that exact reconstruction was independently established.

Human coordinates are from GRCh38, and chimpanzee coordinates from Pan_tro_3.0, using the supplied Ensembl release-116 annotation snapshot. The models retain their own assembly coordinates. They are neither measured expression tracks nor a matched human–chimpanzee phenotype experiment.

Load one offline comparison

The bundled loader constructs a SynSpecies containing two SynIndividual objects, their CDS/UTR annotations, a SynPairAlignment, and stored genomic windows. No network access, LASTZ installation, or working-directory paths are needed to render the tutorial. These helpers are example-level code, not new exported package functions.

library(ggexon)
library(ggplot2)
demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", "as3mt", package = "ggexon")
source(file.path(demo_dir, "load-as3mt-example.R"), local = TRUE)
as3mt <- load_as3mt_example(demo_dir)
as3mt$comparison
#> An object of class "SynSpecies"
#>   name: AS3MT human-chimpanzee transcript comparison 
#>   individuals: 2 
#>   pairwise_alignments: 1 
#>   multiple_alignments: 0 
#>   homology_annotations: 0 
#>   locus_sets: 0 
#>   tree: FALSE 
#>   tree_plot: FALSE

The selected human references are NM_020682.4 / ENST00000369880.8 and NP_065733.2; the selected chimpanzee transcript is ENSPTRT00000007262.6. Original annotation snapshots, sequence hashes, the specification and source cells are preserved under the bundled extdata/as3mt directory.

One full-locus view with smaller introns 

as3mt_plot <- plot_as3mt_example(as3mt, intron_factor = 30)
as3mt_plot$plot

AS3MT transcripts with introns compressed 30-fold.

Gold E2/E3 occur in the human full-length transcript. Dashed outlines mark their skipped positions in d2d3. E1–E4 remain distinguishable without a second zoom panel. Separate exon/intron scale bars state their actual base-pair widths and the compression factor.

Thick boxes show CDS including the stop codon; thin boxes show UTR. Only the two highest LASTZ identity categories are shown. The ungapped DNA blocks contain no within-block indels and do not measure expression. Links follow the exon/intron scale boundaries automatically.

The core grammar used inside the helper is:

ggexon(as3mt$comparison) +
  geom_exon2(
    aes(xmin = xmin - 0.5, xmax = xmax + 0.5,
        ymin = isoform_y, transcripts = transcript_name, fill = exon_class),
    annotation_type = "all", compress_introns = FALSE,
    utr_height = 0.35, cds_height = 1
  ) +
  geom_nuclink(alignment = "human_chimp", aes(fill = identity_band),
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_genomics(vars(track), scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_ggexon_genomic(
    intron_factor = 30,
    guide = guide_x_ggexon_piecewise(by = "panel")
  )

The half-base box edges preserve inclusive exon lengths. Setting compress_introns = FALSE on the geom leaves compression to the scale, avoiding a second schematic transformation.

Links follow the mosaic exon/intron scale

geom_nuclink() automatically splits each link at the union of scale boundaries crossed in either annotation panel. Each resulting piece uses its target panel’s map at one end and its query panel’s map at the other. Changing intron_factor therefore updates both the annotations and links. Raw alignment coordinates remain genomic; no example-specific endpoint conversion is used. Stored genomic windows are also mapped into display limits automatically.

Within an ungapped alignment block this preserves nucleotide correspondence. For general interval-only gapped links, subdivision retains proportional endpoint correspondence; use ungapped blocks when exact internal nucleotide correspondence is needed.

link_layer <- which(vapply(as3mt_plot$plot$layers,
  function(layer) inherits(layer$geom, "GeomPanel"), logical(1)))
vertices <- as3mt_plot$build$data[[link_layer]]
data.frame(
  original_blocks = length(unique(vertices$parent_group)),
  native_polygon_pieces = length(unique(vertices$group))
)
#>   original_blocks native_polygon_pieces
#> 1              37                    57

The 37 original blocks become 57 polygon pieces. Built vertices retain genomic_x, parent_group and link_piece for inspection.

How the alignment was generated

Reference chromosome-10 windows were downloaded from Ensembl and assembly checked: human 102869470–102901899 and chimpanzee 104324156–104356197. The recorded LASTZ 1.04.52 command is:

lastz human.fa chimp.fa --strand=both --nogapped --chain \
  --format=paf:minimap2 --output=human_chimp.nogap.paf

Every one of the 124 raw blocks was checked for a single gap-free CIGAR, equal query/target/alignment spans, and a matching-base count agreeing with the input DNA. Filtering for length ≥80 bp and identity ≥50% retained 93 blocks. The plot keeps only the two highest identity quantile categories: 97.1–98.3% and 98.3–100.0% (rounded labels), totaling 37 blocks. Those category boundaries were calculated before this final selection and were not recalculated afterward. Reverse-strand sequence matches can occur; links are not themselves evidence for exon correspondence or exon skipping.

Anchored DNA differences with geom_alignseq()

Display the experimentally supported exon-1 VNTR

This example focuses on the 36-bp exon-1 tandem repeat (VNTR), which has functional evidence for regulating AS3MTd2d3 splicing. It replaces the arbitrary substitution and one-base indel formerly used to demonstrate sequence drawing.

Li et al. (2016), Supplementary Fig. 3a, identifies the repeat sequence. The supplied handoff maps three exact copies in the selected GRCh38 reference:

v <- readRDS(file.path(demo_dir, "vntr-dna.rds"))
v$motif
#> [1] "CCTGAGTCGCAGGCCGAGGAGACAGTGAGTGCGCGC"
knitr::kable(v$human_units, col.names = c("GRCh38 start", "GRCh38 end", "Repeat"))
GRCh38 start GRCh38 end Repeat
102869498 102869533 1
102869534 102869569 2
102869570 102869605 3

The unit is CCTGAGTCGCAGGCCGAGGAGACAGTGAGTGCGCGC. Each of the three copies was checked base for base against the offline human genomic FASTA. The last copy spans 102869570–102869605: its first 24 bases are in E1, and its last 12 bases are in intron 1. The E1 donor lies between 102869593 and 102869594, immediately before the conserved GT:

CCTGAGTCGCAGGCCGAGGAGACA | GTGAGTGCGCGC
            exon 1      | intron 1

The selected Pan_tro_3.0 reference has one imperfect homologous unit at 104324211–104324246, matching 34 of 36 human bases. Its donor also lies after unit base 24 (between 104324234 and 104324235), with the same GT. This is a single homologous segment, rather than an exact copy of the human motif. An exact-motif search returning zero in chimp would not establish that the homologous sequence is absent.

Functional evidence: two human repeat alleles

Cai et al. tested human two-repeat and three-repeat minigenes, constructed to differ only at the VNTR. The three-repeat constructs produced more d2d3 in the tested cell lines. This is the experimentally supported regulatory variant shown in the figure: repeat-number variation, rather than a demonstrated causal SNV at E2/E3. Cai et al., 2021.

The figure separates the human/chimp reference comparison from this human allele experiment. The selected human reference contains three repeats; it is not a claim that all humans have three. Published human repeat counts include two, three and four. The evidence strip depicts motif-count reconstructions of the tested two/three-repeat contrast, not deposited full plasmid sequences or newly measured expression values. Functional regulation does not by itself establish that this expansion was sufficient for the evolutionary origin of the reported human-specific isoform.

sequence_example <- plot_as3mt_alignseq(demo_dir, intron_factor = 30)
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(sequence_example$grob)

Exon-1 VNTR and the human two-/three-repeat minigene comparison.

Purple outlines identify the repeat units in the genomic annotation. The −72 marker means chimp has 72 fewer aligned repeat bases relative to this human reference. It does not assign ancestral insertion/deletion direction, and it is not the experimentally tested 36-bp difference between two and three human repeats. The two base differences within the chimp homolog are sequence context, not labelled as splicing-causal SNVs.

Human DNA remains on the human annotation panel and chimp DNA on the chimp panel. Smooth connectors retain genomic anchors while equally spaced letters are schematic. The vertical boundary in each sequence row marks the verified E1 donor without altering the DNA. Two scale bars sit below the colour legend: 500 exon bp and 15 intron kb at 30-fold compression have equal displayed lengths, calibrated to the common annotation-panel scale.

How the sequence layer is prepared 

sequence_data <- alignseq_data(
  aligned = v$aligned, anchors = v$anchors, reference = "human",
  regions = v$regions, details = v$details, flank = 0
)
sequence_data$y <- ifelse(sequence_data$sequence == "human", 2.65, 1.5)
sequence_data$boundary_after <- !is.na(sequence_data$position) &
  sequence_data$position == v$donor_after[sequence_data$sequence]
sequence_data$boundary_label <- ifelse(sequence_data$boundary_after,
  "E1 donor | intron 1", "")
# Only repeat-copy difference markers are emphasized; base differences remain
# visible in the terminal-unit sequence as comparative context.
sequence_data$event_id[sequence_data$event_type == "substitution"] <- NA_integer_
as3mt_plot$plot + geom_alignseq(data = sequence_data)

geom_alignseq() takes two prealigned strings, an explicit reference and one one-based genomic anchor per sequence. Gaps (-) do not consume genomic bases. Minus-strand strings must already be oriented for comparison; anchors represent contiguous genomic DNA. Optional boundary_after and boundary_label columns mark verified splice boundaries in the callouts.

This VNTR uses an explicit donor-anchored repeat alignment: the chimp unit aligns to the human terminal, donor-containing unit, with 72 gap columns opposite the other two human copies. Identical repeat copies make equivalent gap placements possible; this alignment does not identify the individual history of the repeated copies. Both ungapped strings were verified against the offline assembly FASTAs. The original longest gapped LASTZ block starts within the human array and is therefore not used to infer the complete VNTR copy difference. It remains bundled separately as aligned-dna.rds for audit; the overview’s ungapped ribbons are unchanged.

Optional row mode: the donor-containing unit

For a short window, mode = "rows" displays every selected base on its own annotation panel. Here each row contains the 36-base terminal unit/homolog. The grey exon segment covers 24 bases and the intron backbone the remaining 12, using each assembly’s genomic coordinates.

sequence_example$rows

short <- alignseq_data(v$aligned, v$anchors, reference = "human",
  regions = v$details)
geom_alignseq(data = short, mode = "rows")

The layer uses GeomText with optional nucleotide backgrounds. Selected nearby detail windows merge when their flanking columns overlap. Omitted columns split callouts; row mode requires one contiguous window. The default maximum detail length is 60 columns; the VNTR terminal unit uses 36.

Transcript, protein and organoid interpretation

The overview’s exon slots are schematic, unlike the assembly-specific, piecewise genomic scale in the comparison above. Skipping E2/E3 removes 169 RNA nucleotides, destroys the original E1/E2-split start codon, and uses the handoff-assigned downstream start in E4. The assigned 273-aa protein corresponds to full-length residues 103–375, losing 102 N-terminal amino acids. This is not a 306-nt in-frame exon deletion. The reconstructed 2,281-nt RNA length is conditional on the selected ends and reference repeat allele.

The organoid data compare control with AS3MTd2d3 overexpression in H9/WA09 human forebrain organoids, electroporated at day 50. Each SOX2 or TUJ1 endpoint has 7 control and 11 overexpression reported values. Points show every supplied percentage; summaries use the arithmetic mean and sample SD divided by √n. The publication does not define the sampling unit: these counts must not be described as independent donors or organoids. The reported two-sided unpaired-t-test P values are 0.0008 for SOX2 and 0.0014 for TUJ1.

summary <- as3mt$organoid_summary
summary$group <- c("Control", "AS3MTd2d3 overexpression")[summary$group]
knitr::kable(summary, digits = 3)
marker group mean sem n
SOX2+ / GFP+ Control 49.692 2.659 7
SOX2+ / GFP+ AS3MTd2d3 overexpression 37.578 1.645 11
TUJ1+ / GFP+ Control 45.184 2.072 7
TUJ1+ / GFP+ AS3MTd2d3 overexpression 60.101 2.768 11

Li et al. did not detect the chimp E1–E4 junction in the examined pooled-tissue RNA-seq, which included brain. This is not proof of absence in every tissue. Healthy humans also express the short isoform; the experiment does not measure species-specific disease rates.

Sources and reproducibility

  • Li et al. (2016), Nature Medicine, doi:10.1038/nm.4096.
  • Cai et al. (2021), Schizophrenia Bulletin, doi:10.1093/schbul/sbaa098, VNTR minigene experiments on AS3MTd2d3 splicing.
  • Kim et al. (2025), Science Advances, doi:10.1126/sciadv.adp8271, Supplementary Fig. S8B–C and Table S5, cells A34:A40 and B34:B44.

The repository’s data-raw/as3mt directory contains the alignment-preparation and figure-export scripts. The loader and all plotting inputs are bundled in the installed package under extdata/as3mt. The optional rat-neuron and spindle-angle panels are not included in these figures.
